title: Variables aren't as scary as they sound.
prerequisites: None. This is the first Python lesson on this site.
minutesNote: Estimate for a first read plus one successful run. Not timed research.
objectives: Say what a variable is, in ordinary language.
Change a value and print again.

quiz.prompt: Which line stores the text Bloomington in a variable called city?
quiz.why: Text needs quotes. print only shows a value. It does not store one.

quiz.prompt: What does print(name) do if name = "Jade" already ran?

options.label: It creates a new variable called print.
It shows Jade, then deletes name.
It shows the value stored in name. name stays.

quiz.why: print looks up the name and writes the value to output. The variable is still there.

quiz.prompt: You write tea = matcha with no quotes. What goes wrong?

options.label: Python looks for a variable named matcha, and usually raises NameError.
Python stores the word matcha anyway.
The programme prints matcha and continues.

quiz.why: Without quotes, matcha is a name, not text. If that name was never assigned, Python stops with NameError.
